name: Aqua Park Shinagawa
desc: Dolphin show with lights and music, plus tanks in the same building. More of a performance than a quiet aquarium. Shows last about 20 minutes. Book a timed show if you care about seats. Price: adults about ¥2,400–¥3,400 by date; children less.

name: teamLab Planets
desc: Barefoot walk through water, digital koi and a flower garden. About 1.5–2 hours. Best hands-on pick for a 10-year-old. No same-day window. Wear shorts you can roll; lockers for shoes. Price: adults from about ¥3,600; ages 4–12 about ¥1,500; under 4 free.

name: teamLab Borderless
desc: Shoes on, no map, maze of light rooms plus Athletic Forest. 2–3 hours. Dry floors. Check Tuesday closures. Less water than Planets; more running around. Price: adults from about ¥3,600; child tickets cheaper; timed booking.

name: New Year Kabuki
desc: January programme at the New National Theatre, Hatsudai. English audio guide for rent. Afternoon slots are easier with jet lag. On sale from 13 Dec 2026. Not ideal for a restless 10-year-old. Price: typically several thousand yen to over ¥10,000 by seat.

name: Ryoko Moriyama
desc: Folk / pop concert at Nippon Budokan on 7 Jan. Ticketed seated show. Confirm doors and age policy on the official page. Not a kids’ event unless the child already likes her music. Price: paid concert ticket; see the official sale.

name: Yomiuri Nippon Symphony
desc: Orchestra Series No.58, Tokyo Performing Music Festival. Friday 8 Jan 2027, 19:00, Tokyo Metropolitan Theatre Concert Hall. Preschoolers are usually not admitted. Single tickets from 10 Nov 2026. Price: festival orchestra seats are typically a few thousand yen (often ¥2,000–¥5,000).

name: ORANGE RANGE
desc: J-rock / pop concert at NHK Hall, Shibuya, 9 Jan. Loud, ticketed, standing or reserved depending on the bill. Confirm the official sale and door time. Price: paid concert ticket.

name: LiSA
desc: J-pop / anime-song live, 9–10 Jan at TOYOTA Arena Tokyo, Aomi. Two nights, usually sells out. New waterfront arena. Fine for a 10-year-old who already knows the songs; use hearing protection. Price: paid concert ticket; check the official sale.

name: TCB comedy
desc: Tokyo Comedy Bar stand-up in Shibuya. Some nights are English-friendly. Confirm the 9 Jan lineup. 21+ is common for evening rooms — check before bringing a child. Price: cover plus drink, often about ¥2,000–¥4,000.

name: Musée d’Orsay exhibition
desc: “Joy of living” works from the Musée d’Orsay at Tokyo Metropolitan Art Museum. Indoor adult show next to Ueno Zoo. 60–90 minutes. Advance tickets cut the door queue. Price: special exhibition ticket, typically about ¥2,000 adults; students less.

name: Yokohama Illumination
desc: City-wide winter lights along Minato Mirai. Yorunoyo’s big 2026 show ends 30 Dec; waterfront trees continue into February. Free 30–60 minute evening walk. About 30 min from Tokyo Station. Price: free.

name: Cup Noodles Museum
desc: Design your own cup and walk the factory displays. High school and under free entry; the custom-cup workshop is extra and timed. 10:00–18:00. Next to Cosmo World. About 1–1.5 hours. Price: adult entry about ¥500; workshop extra (often about ¥500–¥800).

name: Yokohama Cosmo World
desc: Ferris wheel and small rides on the Minato Mirai waterfront. Pay per ride or buy a pass. Easy with Cup Noodles and Red Brick Warehouse. The Cosmo Clock 21 wheel is the signature photo. Price: per-ride tickets or a day pass; wheel alone is a few hundred yen.

name: Hakkeijima Sea Paradise
desc: Large aquarium, dolphin and beluga shows, plus an amusement park. Full-day kid trip. Winter outdoor rides may pause in wind. One train past central Yokohama. Price: Aqua Museum / passport typically about ¥3,000–¥5,500 by package.

name: Yokohama Chinatown
desc: Food streets, gates, Hikawa Maru nearby, Landmark Tower views. Chinese New Year festival starts 20 Jan — after this week. Budget for snacks rather than an entry fee. Price: free to walk; meals ¥1,000–¥2,000 per person.

name: Joma Shinji archery
desc: Archers shoot a target painted as a “demon” at Tsurugaoka Hachimangu. Samurai-era New Year rite. Stand with the crowd on the shrine grounds. Morning of 5 Jan; dress for outdoor cold. Price: free to watch.

name: Hatsu Kagura
desc: First kagura dance of the year at small Yakumo Shrine, Omachi. Short local ceremony. Easy to miss if you arrive late. Combine with the Hachimangu walk the same day. Price: free.

name: Dai-shime Festival
desc: Giant shimenawa rope offering in centipede form, for harvest and safety. Hakusan Shrine, 8 Jan. Outdoor, 30–60 minutes. More local than touristy. Price: free.

name: Hon Ebisu
desc: Ebisu festival at Hongakuji: fuku-musume hand out lucky mochi and sake charms. Busy, cheerful, and short. 10 Jan. Sake charms are for adults; mochi is the kid-friendly bit. Price: free to watch; charms cost a small fee if you buy one.

name: Shio matsuri (Sakanoshita)
desc: Sea rite for safe fishing at Sakanoshita Beach. Cold outdoor morning on 11 Jan. Dress warm and waterproof. Pair with the Zaimokuza kagura the same morning. Price: free.

name: Shio kagura (Zaimokuza)
desc: Kagura on the sand for sea safety, Zaimokuza Beach, 11 Jan. Same morning as Sakanoshita. Short and windswept. Bring a warm layer; there is little shelter. Price: free.

name: Great Buddha (Kotoku-in)
desc: Kamakura’s bronze Daibutsu in Hase. You can step inside the statue for a little extra. Easy day from Tokyo (~1 hour). Combine with a dated shrine rite. About 30–45 minutes on site. Price: grounds about ¥300; inside the statue a little extra.

name: Hasedera
desc: Kannon temple with hillside gardens and a view of Yuigahama. Next to the Great Buddha. Hydrangeas are off-season; the view still works. Allow 45–60 minutes. Price: about ¥400.

name: Edo-Tokyo Museum
desc: Reopened after renovation. Life-size Nihonbashi and Edo streets. Pair with sumo at Ryogoku. Maruyama Okyo special through 24 Jan 2027. 2 hours for a curious 10-year-old. Price: permanent collection about ¥600 adults; special exhibit extra.

name: National Museum of Nature and Science
desc: Dinosaurs, blue whale, two galleries. Best indoor kid museum this week. School-age entry is often free. 11 Jan holiday should be open. 2–3 hours if they like skeletons. Price: adults ¥630; high school and under usually free.

name: Tokyo National Museum
desc: Largest collection in Japan: armor, sculpture, lacquer. The Genji special starts 19 Jan, after this week. Honkan plus one garden stroll is enough. Price: regular exhibition ¥1,000 adults; students less; under-18 often free or reduced.

name: Mori Art Museum
desc: Contemporary art on Mori Tower 53F plus Tokyo City View. Easy with Midtown skating and teamLab Borderless. Sunset view is the extra treat. Price: exhibition + view combo typically about ¥2,000–¥2,800 adults.

name: Tokyo Toy Museum
desc: Wooden toys and play rooms in a former elementary school, Yotsuya. Hands-on, 1–2 hours. Closed Thursdays — closed 7 Jan 2027. Best indoor play option if Ghibli tickets are gone. Price: about ¥800–¥1,000 adults; children similar or a little less.

name: Shin-Yokohama Ramen Museum
desc: Showa street downstairs and regional ramen counters. Pair with the skate center. One bowl is the visit. Can be crowded at lunch; go mid-afternoon. Price: entry about ¥400–¥500; ramen extra (about ¥1,000).

name: Kamakura National Treasure Museum
desc: Temple sculptures and treasures, often without glass. Small visit next to Tsurugaoka Hachimangu. 20–40 minutes. Good if the shrine rite is short. Price: about ¥400.

name: Zeniarai Benten
desc: Cave shrine where you wash coins in spring water for luck. Kids like the tunnel, the water and the egg offerings for the snake god. Open 8:00–16:30, last entry 16:00. The first-snake festival is 2 Jan 2027, before this week. From Kamakura west exit about 25 minutes on foot. Price: free grounds; donation, and a small fee if you rent a wash basket.

name: Azumayama Park (Ninomiya)
desc: Hill above JR Ninomiya with early rapeseed, Sagami Bay and, on a clear day, Mount Fuji. About 20 minutes of stairs from the north exit (Yakuba-guchi). Park 8:30–17:00. Peak yellow is mid-January; 5–9 Jan can still be thin. From Kamakura about 30 minutes on the Tokaido line. Price: free.

name: Cat Cafe MOCHA Shibuya
desc: Walk-in cat cafe on Center Gai, about 29 cats, drink bar and manga. Ages 3+; under junior high need an adult. Weekdays about ¥297 per 10 minutes, cap about ¥3,960; weekends higher. 45–60 minutes is enough. No booking. Price: time charge plus optional ¥550 cat treats.

name: Cat Cafe MOCHA Ikebukuro
desc: One minute from Ikebukuro west exit. Ages 6+ with an adult if under junior high. Same time-charge system as Shibuya, drink bar included. Easy with Sunshine Aquarium. Cats are mostly pedigree breeds. Price: about ¥297 per 10 minutes weekdays, cap about ¥3,960; weekends about ¥385 / ¥4,620.

name: Temari no Ouchi
desc: Storybook cat cafe near Kichijoji station, often paired with Ghibli and Inokashira Zoo. Flat stay fee rather than a ticking clock; check that day’s rate on the shop page. Some rooms ask for about age 10. Food and tea on the menu. Price: typically about ¥1,200–¥1,600 stay; confirm on the official page.

name: mipig cafe Harajuku
desc: Reservation-only micro-pig cafe, 10:00–20:00. Arrive 10 minutes early; no walk-ins. Ages 4+ pay ¥3,300 for 25 minutes or ¥4,950 for 55 minutes; ages 3 and under ¥1,100. Private rooms extra. Book on the official Harajuku page. Price: as above; no extra drink listed on the current tariff.
